name: fur pile
label: beodeul_city/wave-places/ice-age-field/fur_pile
reasons: 화풍: 윤곽이 근흑(재질 어두운 톤 아님) (4/4)

surfaces.part: front face (brown and grey fur layers)

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a low mound that widens from 8 px at row 4 to 13 px at rows 11-13. Rows 4-6 are a pale, near-white band that works as the heap's upper surface. Row 7 is a darker line (#665a52 / #4a403a) followed by dark row 8 (#302824), which acts as a front-edge line with shadow. Below that, rows 9-14 are a brown band, a light grey band and a dark base. These read as the front face of the heap, about 8 rows tall. The top is short and the layering is stripe-like, so this is borderline, but the pale top band with an edge line and shadow gives a top surface plus a front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny pile, roughly 11x8 source pixels, much smaller than the references. It reads as a grey-white mound with a dark rim and a few light and brown banding strokes, so I count about 3 lightness steps against 5-6 on the well roof, hedge and stall. 89% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline is a near-black sticker line. The references that use tinted outlines (hedge 0%, stall 1%) show the dark-material-tone craft this piece lacks. The tile-based facts are 0 because the piece is under one tile, so I judged by eye. It has no per-clump fur strands, tonal clusters or grain like the hedge's leaf clumps, and it looks thinner and flatter than the hedge or well at the same scale. It is not a flat-fill failure only because the area is small. The shallow shading, neutral outline and low richness together make it fail.

surfaces.part: white fur heap on top of the pile
grey/cream pelt layer with its own edge line and shadow

answer.evidence: The silhouette grows from 8 px wide at row 4 to 13 px at rows 11-13, a mound shape. Rows 4-6 are a white fur heap that ends at a lighter grey edge at row 6, then dark shadow at rows 7-8 (L=93, 42-66). Below that is a front face of about 7 rows (8-14). It is brown at rows 9-11 and has a light edge line at row 12 with darker rows 13-14 under it. This is a heap with a visible top and a front face, so I read it as three_quarter. The top is small at 3-4 rows and the stacked layers are only weakly separated.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny pile (about 20x14 px, smaller than one tile) of grey-white and brown layers, so the per-tile tone facts are 0 and I judged by eye. It shows about 3 lightness steps: a light top, a mid band and a dark base. There is no per-fur grain, tuft, or clump variation like the hedge's leaf clumps or the well's stones. 89% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline is a near-black rim, close to the sticker look. The references use tinted dark tones (hedge 0% neutral, stall 1%). Next to the hedge, stall and well, the pile looks thinner and flatter, with much less information per area. It is small but not rich, so it fails.

surfaces.part: white fur tuft on top of the mound

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a mound that widens steadily from 8 px wide at row 4 to 13 px at rows 11-13, then narrows to 11 px at row 14. The column scan shows horizontal colour bands stacked down the face: white at rows 5-6, dark brown and orange-brown at rows 7-11, a light grey line at row 12, and dark grey at rows 13-14. These bands read as a side view of layered fur. No back-to-front ellipse or widening-then-narrowing top plane is visible. There is also no front-edge line with eave shadow beneath it. The white rows at the top are only 1-2 rows tall and look like a highlight on the crest, not a horizontal surface. The object is mostly a front face of about 9 rows, so it reads as front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny pile, smaller than one 16x16 tile, so the per-tile tone count is 0 and I judged density by eye. It reads as a pale top, a mid tone and a dark base, about 3 visible steps, against roughly 5-6 on the well roof and stall awning. It has 17 raw colours, which is not much for its size, and some speckle on the top. 89% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline is a grey-black line around the whole shape, the sticker look. The hedge and stall references have 0-1% neutral edges, and the well has 33%. The lamp's 100% is a thin pole, so it is not a fair comparison. Next to the richer references (well, stall, hedge) it looks thinner and flatter, so a careful artist would not accept it as equal.

surfaces.part: middle brown fur layer, front face
lower grey-brown fur layer, front face

answer.evidence: The silhouette widens from 8 px at row 4 to 13 px at rows 11-13, then narrows to 11 px at row 14, which gives a mound shape. Rows 4-6 are a light white/grey fur heap top. Row 7 is a darker line (L about 66-93) that acts as the front edge, and row 8 is dark shadow (L about 42). Below that, rows 8-14 are the front face, made of a brown band at rows 9-11 and a grey-brown band at rows 12-14. This gives a top plus a front face of about 7 rows. The top is a loose heap with no hard edges, so the call is borderline, but it reads as three_quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny pile, smaller than one 16x16 tile, so the per-tile tone count is 0 and I judged density by eye. It has 17 distinct colours in total. The pile reads as a light top over a darker body, so I count about 3 usable lightness steps on the fur ramp. The references (bench, well, stall) show 5-6 steps. 89% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, which points to a grey/black sticker-style outline. The tinted references (hedge 0%, stall 1%) lean toward the material instead. The bench is also small but has a tinted outline (44% neutral) and wood grain. Fur has no clump or strand texture and no per-tuft highlights. The measured facts show no flat fills, but the piece is still thinner and more sticker-like than the references.
